Reasoning.description: Seating arrangement, blood relations, inequalities, coding-decoding, floor puzzle

question_types.example: Fourteen persons sit in two parallel rows. Row-1: A,B,C,D,E,F,G face north. Row-2: P,Q,R,S,T,U,V face south. V is the only immediate neighbour of S. T sits 2nd to the left of V.
Statements: P > Q = R >= S < T, U <= S > W. Conclusions: I. P > T  II. W < P
question_types.options_style: (a) Only I true (b) Only II true (c) Either I or II (d) Neither (e) Both true

question_types.example: Q is the only daughter of R who is the mother-in-law of U. S is the paternal grandfather of Q's nephew.
question_types.options_style: (a) Mother (b) Aunt (c) Uncle (d) Mother-in-law (e) None of these

question_types.example: Ten persons N,O,P,Q,R,S,T,U,V,W live in a five-story building. Each floor has Flat-X (west) and Flat-Y (east).
question_types.options_style: (a) Floor 1 (b) Floor 2 (c) Floor 3 (d) Floor 4 (e) None of these

question_types.example: 'happy not bad good towards' coded as 'xa pb ut nq tf'. 'good smile sorrow towards' coded as 'ut tf rd lk'.
question_types.options_style: (a) xa (b) rd (c) nq (d) pb (e) None of these

question_types.example: Seven persons M,N,O,P,Q,R,S sit in a row facing north. Each likes different fruits: Apple, Banana, Mango, Orange, Grapes, Pineapple, Watermelon.
question_types.options_style: (a) Banana (b) Pineapple (c) Apple (d) Grapes (e) None of these

Quantitative.description: Number series, data interpretation, arithmetic problems

question_types.example: Pie chart shows orders by Twiggy and Xomato. Total=720. Thursday=20%, Friday=15%, Saturday=40%, Sunday=25%.
A invests Rs P at 5% p.a. for 2 years SI. B invests Rs P+1000 at 10% p.a. for 3 years SI. Difference = 1300.
Article marked up 30% above CP, sold at 10% discount. Profit = Rs 204. Find SP at 10% profit.
A and B together complete work in 6 days. Time for A to do 90% = Time for B to do 60%. Find time for A to do 50%.

English.description: Reading comprehension, error detection, fill in the blanks

question_types.example: Find grammatical error in the sentence
question_types.options_style: (a) Part A (b) Part B (c) Part C (d) Part D (e) No error

question_types.example: The committee _____ the proposal after a long discussion.
question_types.options_style: (a) approved (b) approving (c) approve (d) had approve (e) None

question_types.example: FELICITOUS - use 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 6th letters to form meaningful word
